content.title: About
content.content: The chicken drumstick is the lower part of the leg, consisting of meat, bone, and skin. It is commonly cooked whole, often with the skin left on, which becomes crispy and flavorful when properly prepared.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are a staple in dishes that require juiciness and rich flavor, such as barbecues, roasts, and fried chicken.
The skin is rich in collagen, which turns into a crunchy crust during cooking.
The NS (no‑fat grill) method preserves maximum taste and nutrients while reducing added fat.
Drumsticks can be split into thigh and lower leg portions for easy portioning.
Different cuisines treat drumsticks uniquely: Asian recipes often marinate them in soy sauce, while Western styles coat them with spices and bake.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals help maintain immune health and hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Skin supplies healthy fats
items.content: When eaten in moderation, the skin offers monounsaturated fats and cholesterol needed for hormonal balance.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Drumsticks fit well into low‑carb dietary patterns.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: High sodium in marinades
items.content: Excessively salty marinades can increase sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Chicken protein allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Caloric skin
items.content: The skin adds calories and fat; those monitoring weight should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken drumsticks can be baked, fried, grilled (NS), or braised. When cooking with skin, pat it dry, lightly brush with oil, season, and cook until golden and crisp. Serve with vegetables, sauces, or as part of dishes like chicken wings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh drumsticks in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen drumsticks store at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen pieces in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
